title: prefill/decode: chunked speculative prefill + kernel scheduler + KV-cache batching optimizations
author: Ravi Kapoor
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token latency and increase throughput for mixed prefill+decode workloads by overlapping stages and making prefill incremental/chunked with speculative outputs. This PR implements three coordinated optimizations: 1) chunked prefill that splits long prefix prefill into sized chunks and exposes early KV cache availability for downstream decode tasks; 2) speculative prefill that performs lightweight prefix scoring to allow the decode stage to begin on high-confidence cache state earlier; 3) kernel scheduler and KV-cache continuous batching adjustments to better prioritize overlapping prefill and decode kernels and reduce idle GPU time. Changes include runtime scheduling policies, a new chunked prefill module, KV-cache manager batching improvements, and small decoder-side changes to consume partial prefill state. Benchmarks: end-to-end throughput +18-25% on mixed workloads with long prefixes, p50 latency down by ~12%, p95 down by ~20-30% on representative internal bench suites. See related Linear tasks ENG-3210 and PERF-298. The description below summarizes commits, changed areas, CI and review thread.

release_notes: Performance: Add chunked and speculative prefill with scheduler and KV-cache batching optimizations. Improves mixed prefill+decode throughput and reduces tail latency. Tunables: prefill.chunk_size (default 512 tokens), prefill.speculative_confidence (default 0.85), scheduler.overlap_policy (default enabled).
notes: This PR is part of a multi-PR rollout coordinated with ENG-3210. Follow-ups: auto-tuning of chunk_size, expanded perf matrix for different GPU generations, and a post-release monitoring dashboard for partial-KV fallbacks.
